exchanges: Hi there. I have a quiet hour while the kids are at practice, so I thought I'd think out loud with you.
A quiet hour is precious. What's on your mind?
Mostly the school play. Ezra got a part in The Wizard of Oz and he's beside himself.
That's wonderful! Which part did he get?
The Lion! He's been roaring around the house for two days.
Perfect for a kid who's already roaring. That part gets some great songs.
He does. Rehearsals are after school on Wednesdays with Mr. Castellanos, the drama teacher.
Weekly rehearsals sound manageable. Is Mr. Castellanos new?
No, he's been there forever. He directed my nephew's play years ago.
A long-time drama teacher usually knows how to bring out the best in kids.
Noor is jealous, of course. She's in grade 3 and the play is only for grades 5 and up.
Her turn will come. Maybe she could help with sets or posters?
That's a good idea, she loves drawing. Her teacher, Ms. Fatima, has been out sick for two weeks though.
Two weeks is a long time. Do you know if she's okay?
It turned out to be pneumonia. She's recovering, but there's a supply teacher until November.
That takes a while to shake off. I hope she's back soon.
Me too. Noor misses her terribly. The supply teacher is fine but strict.
Kids feel those changes. It says a lot that Noor misses her.
Speaking of Fatimas, my sister-in-law Fatima is coming for dinner on Sunday. The kids call her Auntie Fati.
Two in one week. Sunday dinner sounds nice.
It will be. I need to plan the menu carefully because she has type 1 diabetes and counts everything.
That's thoughtful planning. She'll probably have good ideas about what works best.
She's very relaxed about it, which helps. She just brings her own dessert.
That makes it easy for everyone.
Ezra's other thing is chess club. He's been playing a boy named Ji-ho who keeps beating him.
A tough opponent is the fastest way to get better.
That's what I tell him. Ji-ho's mother, Soo-ah, and I have become friends at pickup.
Pickup friendships are underrated. Does she have other kids at the school?
A little one in kindergarten. She runs a florist shop on Elm Street.
That must be a lovely place to work.
She gave me a bouquet for my birthday and it lasted three weeks.
That's the advantage of knowing someone in the business.
Oh, I need to correct something. Ezra isn't the Lion. That's his friend Oliver's part, and Ezra has been practising the roar with him. Ezra is the Scarecrow.
An easy mix-up with all that roaring. Is Ezra happy with his part?
Very happy. He gets to fall over a lot, which is his favourite thing.
A part with lots of falling over is ideal for a kid his age.
I'm going to have to make the costume, which means straw everywhere.
Raffia might be less messy than real straw.
Good tip. My husband, Idris, offered to help, but he's colour-blind and once sent Noor out in two different shoes.
He gets points for trying. Maybe give him the cutting jobs.
Ha, yes. He works nights as a security guard at the hospital, so he's mostly free during the day.
Daytime help is useful for costume making.
True. Noor wants to make a poster for the play. She asked if she can use glitter.
Glitter posters are always a hit.
Absolutely not in the living room, though.
Fair. A spot that's easy to sweep is better.
We'll do it on the deck.
That works, as long as it isn't windy.
Good point.
Glitter and wind don't mix.
Ezra just came home and said Oliver is moving to Montreal after the play. He's heartbroken.
That's hard, especially after doing the play together. When do they leave?
Over Christmas break. His dad got a new job there.
At least they'll have the play first. That'll be a good memory to share.
Ezra wants to make him a goodbye card already.
That's sweet. Kids that age feel friendships deeply.

questions.message: What's Noor's teacher been off with?
What does Soo-ah do for work?
Ezra's playing the Lion, right? I'm telling my mom about the costume.
Where are Oliver and his family relocating?
What does my sister-in-law Fatima do for work?
Maybe we'll make the card together tonight after dinner.
